Microsoft, industry (Li during internship, Gao, Lin, Lin, Rajmohan, Zhang); Nanjing University (Fang, Feng, Liu); University College London (Ye); Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Zhao)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — LOOPSBENCH, a long-horizon benchmark of 112 tasks structured as dependency DAGs of separately testable development units, with a flow-aware runtime that releases tests along the ready frontier and keeps completed units as regression obligations; compares models and loop implementations (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, OpenHands, SWE-agent, mini-SWE-agent, goal modes, dynamic workflows, Ralph loop)

No SDD approach. Loop implementations (versions not stated): Claude Code (via Anthropic Agent SDK), Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenHands, SWE-agent, mini-SWE-agent, Qwen Code; RQ3 loop profiles: Codex goal mode, Claude Code goal mode, Claude Code dynamic workflows, Ralph loop. Models: GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, gpt-5.4 (azure/gpt-5.4-20260305), GPT-5.5, Sonnet-4, Sonnet-4.5, Opus-4.5, Opus-4.7, GLM-5.1, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Qwen2.5-72B, Qwen3-Max, Qwen3.5-Plus, Qwen3.6-Plus, Kimi-2.6, Grok-4.1-FR. Outer continuation (outer evaluation loop, default 3 rounds) as a factor

Benchmark artefacts: per-task bundle with base codebase, global task instruction and per-unit requirement manifests (requirement, file/symbol scope, parents, attached tests), unit DAG, Dockerfile/docker-compose, run-tests.sh, gold patches (hidden). Agent contract: commit one requirement at a time and write requirement_patches/<slug>.diff; optional plan.json DAG (required in RQ2 plan-fidelity runs); optional agent tests; final summary of requirement coverage

Construction: task collection, preprocessing, selection, development-unit definition and DAG recovery, instrumentation (instruction formalization, environment and test synthesis with fail-to-pass trials). Run: loop reads all requirements, optionally plans a DAG, implements and commits unit by unit; runtime snapshots the workspace and releases tests along the ready frontier, keeping passed tests as regression obligations; outer loop restarts with residual work (default 3 rounds)
None (autonomous runs; checkpoint state hidden from the agent). Authors note generated code still requires human review, security testing and licensing checks
N/A (no SDD approach); full autonomous agent loops on the benchmark
Not classifiable (benchmark of agent loops; requirement manifests are inputs; no SDD terms used by the authors)
Mixed: existing code bases (PR Sequences from a base commit) and course-lab skeletons and research-code evolutions; long-horizon multi-unit development

112 tasks (29 PR Sequences, 57 Course Labs, 26 Research Evolutions), more than 5,300 development units, median dependency depth 6; selection requires temporal span >= 2.5 months and solution scale >= 1,200; base repositories from about 80 LoC up to 533k LoC (hadoop_seg05; ClickHouse 511k, Jenkins 494k); median gold patch size 5,499 (Fig. 1); wall-clock budget per task >= 2 h, up to 24 h

9 domains: PR Sequences (infra and data, backend, frontend), Course Labs (game engines, systems, apps and ML), Research Evolutions (analysis and verification, systems and networking, compiler with database and ML); 8 programming languages (not listed in the text)
N/A (no human participants)

Automatic: dual-container snapshot pipeline (container A workspace, container B tests) runs released tests at snapshots triggered by diff growth (min_diff_lines=5), writing observation_history.jsonl; plan.json and requirement patches parsed from the workspace; loop traces and usage from adapter logs (e.g. claude_sdk_trajectory.jsonl); figure scripts read archived JSON without manual entry

Tasks: all 112 tasks (RQ3 goal-mode and Ralph runs on 102 scheduled tasks). Configurations: within-family model scaling under the vendor loop (GPT/Codex, Claude/Claude Code, Qwen/Qwen Code); model sweep under fixed Claude Code loop (8 models); loop sweep under fixed gpt-5.4 (6 loops); RQ3 four loop profiles with their native models. Held constant: task contract and prompt (Benchmark Contract plus profile addendum per adapter class), Docker environment, wall-clock budget per task, outer_loop_count 3, provider defaults except recorded overrides (Claude Code max_tokens 128,000; SWE-agent temperature 0). Acceptance tests: released unit tests, fail-to-pass validated against gold patches, with regression obligations. Repetitions: one trial per pairing (n_attempts 1); pass@3 for within-family pairings only. Human intervention: none

Best: Claude Code + Opus-4.7, 25.00% RR with outer continuation (16.96% without). Within-family RR increases monotonically with model generation, preserved under pass@3. Under fixed gpt-5.4, closed-source loops (Codex 18.75%, Claude Code 17.86%, Copilot 15.18%) above open-source loops (OpenHands 9.82%, SWE-agent 8.93%, mini-swe-agent 7.14%); closed loops have higher plan fidelity (Edge F1 0.58-0.71 vs 0.27-0.39) but more regression (4.83-7.11% vs 0.24-2.46%). Outer continuation raises RR in every configuration. PR Sequences hardest (max 3.45% RR); Course Labs account for >= 70% of resolved tasks. RQ3: dynamic workflows highest RR (24.11%), Ralph lowest (7.84%), described as observed profiles, not causal. No significance tests

Distinguished models and loops (RR 0% to 25%) and exposed plan, implementation and testing differences through trace metrics. Authors: one trial per pairing, pass@3 confirms within-family ordering; RQ3 values are not a model-controlled causal comparison; low Reg in weak configurations reflects few obligations; recovered DAG is a lower bound; hidden checkpoint state mixes limited feedback with regression discipline; proprietary outputs may drift, exact outputs not reproducible

Recovered DAG is a lower bound and may miss implicit dependencies; fixed DAG excludes exploratory redesign; pool limited to sources with auditable prerequisite evidence (mobile, frontend-heavy, hardware-adjacent projects out of scope); metrics tied to the released test suite, not full semantic equivalence; model-assisted materialization may bias wording, boundaries and tests; contamination risk from public sources; internal events outside loop interfaces not measurable; evaluation costly; benchmark measures one executable contract, not general SE ability or deployment readiness. Gap: long-horizon progress limited by global plan maintenance, state continuity and regression obligation retention

Benchmark construction uses Claude Code with Claude Opus 4.7. No pre-registration. Programming languages: 8, not listed (examples Python, Go, Java, Rust)
